Prototype The avatar, four questions from round HS

The centre column is for the graphic

His words: "The center column is sacrosanct for art. Not for text. The right column is for text. The bottom underneath the art is for text. Or design. The left is for a tools." Below: the real Avatar tab as it ships, then the same screen with the law applied. Same pairs. The shot reads 0% because a profile made for the shot keeps no starting weight; the drawing uses the 13, 16 and 24 percent round HG's own shot of these pairs read.

As it ships

What the boxes mark

  1. 1The centre column. 922 pixels wide with the left column open.
  2. 2The graphic: the ring of seven areas. 440 pixels wide, 17 words.
  3. 3A text panel beside the graphic, in the same band, inside the centre column. 418 pixels wide, 92 words. This is the card he named: "do not sideline them by a panel."
  4. 4Text above the graphic, 36 words. The law names text below the art and does not name text above it, so this one is his to rule.
  5. 5The right column, the one meant for text. It shows the Energetic Summary, which is not about the avatar.

The law applied to this screen

What moved

  • The pair panel went right, into the one detail host the right column already carries. Nothing sits beside the ring.
  • The two lines and the release went left. Both write something, so both are tools.
  • The pairs written went below the art. That band is for text or design.
  • Every label that names a concept wears its symbol, including the fetter fear, which ships today as a bare word.

Should the 63 questions feed the avatar?

His words: "Should the 63 questions intake feed the avatar's field? It's a great question. Um, mock that up." Three ways, drawn on one person. Angela, a reference profile, level 5 on the buyer grid. Her answers put Truth at 2.6, Humility at 2.1 and Accountability at 3.2, each out of 10. The Voice area, at the throat, is selected in all three. She has written nothing there.

The team's recommendation: B

  • It joins the two without writing anything. The answers are drawn where the avatar is being worked on. The person decides what, if anything, to write about them.
  • It builds on what exists. The intake already scores each law. No new field on the record, so no schema change.
  • C nominates a lack. A chip under "From your answers" reading "Truth, the throat, 2.6" tells a person where they fall short, and asks them to write about it. The Bible names a false positive on the lack side as the one error the product cannot afford (6.4, item 13). James, who closes the tab on anything that accuses, is the person it loses.
  • Not drawn, and refused: the answers writing the words of a pair. The product may find, cut and mark a person's words. It may not write them (Bible 9.4).

Two archetypes on one page

His words: "Two archetypes exist in the same page. I don't understand that. I need context." The real Avatar tab, scrolled to the wheel, with the left column open. Four places name archetypes on this one screen. Only one of them changes the reading.

What each one is

WhereWhat it isKeptMoves the readingMoves the avatar
1Left column, Primary and SecondaryThe archetypes you pick as yours. Here: Warrior and Sage.In the recordYes. It builds the blueprint ring, which sets how strongly each of the 112 addresses takes chargeNo
2Right column, Archetypes, first to third. Also the glow on the wheel's marksPick 1, read back. It is computed from the picks and the blueprint domains, not from any story.Not kept. Computed each timeNoNo
3Centre, the wheel and the one to five scaleHow much of each archetype is you, one to five. Round HG. Here: Caregiver 4, Magician 2.Beside the record, on this device onlyNo. Nothing in the engine reads itOnly the icon at the ring's core
4Centre, under the scale"Your field reads Warrior first." It sets 3 against 2, and 2 is 1 read back.

Measured on this profile: the reading puts Warrior at 1.00 and Sage at 0.72, the two picks. Innocent reads 0.71, from a blueprint domain. So the sentence in 4 compares what you rated against what you picked, and calls the pick your field.

Ways it could go. His call

1. One input

The one to five scale becomes the archetype input and builds the blueprint ring. The left column's picks go.

Costs: the ratings move into the record, which is a schema change and his. Every reading moves once, on the day it switches.

2. Two inputs, kept apart

The picks stay as the blueprint, the scale stays as the avatar's. Neither is shown as a reading of the other, so 2 and 4 stop calling the pick your field.

Costs: a person still meets the twelve twice on one tab, with two meanings.

3. The field reads its own

The scale stays as the person's own say. The field's archetype read comes from what the stories carry, so 4 becomes a real comparison.

Costs: new engine work. No story reads an archetype today.

True under all three: sentence 4 is not a field reading, and it should not say it is. That changes no mechanism.

The archetype wheel, with one selected

His words: "these radial designs, I like them, I don't understand them, like if you've got caregiver selected, so many things happening."

What goes, and why

  1. 1The seven coloured arcs and seven area icons inside the wheel. They are the avatar ring's seven areas, drawn a second time. One graphic, one job.
  2. 2The glow on each mark. It is the left column's pick read back (see Two archetypes). It returns only if he rules that the pick is the reading.
  3. 3The area name under the core. The colour and the icon already carry the seat.
  4. 4"Primary saboteur, at the heart." The saboteur's own symbol and colour carry it.
  5. 5"One press sets it. The same press again takes it off." It describes the control, which a section may not do (Bible 1.4).
  6. 6"Your field reads Warrior first." It compares the scale with the pick. Held until the two archetypes question is ruled.

What stays: the twelve, each with its icon and name; the number a person set, as a pill; the selection; one sentence on what the archetype does; the saboteur it runs with, with its symbol and one sentence on what it costs. The scale moves to the left column, because it writes.

Choices do not fall, and should not: twelve archetypes and five points are the roster and his scale. Hick's law prices a choice among twelve at about 3.7 bits either way. What he is reacting to is what the eye sorts before it can choose. The wheel meant seven things at once (archetype, area arc, area icon, glow, rating, selection, core seat) and now means three (archetype, rating, selection).
